To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the hole-trapping by Al-dopants in BaTiO3 is thermally activated with the energy of 1.04 e.V and that it is responsible for the observed nonstoichiometric behavior and the anomalous temperature dependence of conductivity, chemical diffusion, oxygen vacancy concentration, etc. in Al-doped BaTi03.

the equilibrium constant for the hole-trapping reaction by acceptor dopants in BaTiO3 is evaluated as Ka=1.9 x10(23)exp(-1.04eV/kT)cm(-3) and that the mobility of trapped carriers is much lower than that of free carriers.
hole-trapping is a key factor in determining the mass/charge transport and defect properties of acceptor-doped perovskites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of hole-traps in the acceptor-doping of BaTiO3 on the transport properties of the material.
the equilibrium and non-equilibrium properties of the acceptor- and donor-doped systems in the context of the hole-trapping effect.
the effect of hole trapping on the mass and charge transport properties in acceptors-doped BaTi0(3) and the results are compared with the previous studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hole-trapping by the acceptor-dopant (Al) is the most plausible mechanism to account for the experimental data on Al-doped BaTi03.
the trapping of holes by Al-dopants is a major factor that governs the equilibrium conductivity, chemical diffusion and oxygen nonstoichiomtry in Al-doped BaTi0(3).
the hole-trapping effect in acceptor-doping is a very important factor that should not be neglected for understanding the mass transport properties and defect chemistry in acceptor-dopant systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hole-trapping effect is important in acceptor-doping of oxides with a wide bandgap.
the hole-trapping effect should be taken into account to interpret the transport properties of acceptor-doped perovskite oxides.
the hole-trapping is the most important factor for the mass/charge transport of acceptor-doped perovskite oxides.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the trapping effect is important in the interpretation of the equilibrium properties of acceptor-doped oxides and that the hole-trapping effect should not be neglected in the analysis of the transport properties of acceptor impurity-doped oxides.
the hole-trapping effect should be taken into account for quantitative analysis of the equilibrium conductivity and chemical transport of acceptor-doped perovskite-type oxides.
the hole-trapping effect should be considered for a proper interpretation of mass/charge transport in acceptor-dope BaTiO3 and related oxides.
